quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'only' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The coupon applies only to online purchases, not in-store ones.
quests.hint: A common mistake is placing this word right before the main verb - instead, place it directly before the specific thing it's limiting.
quests.explanation: Placing 'only' before 'applies' would wrongly suggest nothing else about the coupon is true. It belongs directly before 'to online purchases', the exact thing being limited.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'almost' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The team finished almost every task before the deadline.
quests.hint: A common mistake is placing this word right before the verb, which would suggest they finished nothing - instead, place it before the quantity word it limits.
quests.explanation: Placing 'almost' before 'finished' would suggest the team came close to finishing but perhaps completed very little. Placed before 'every task', it correctly shows most, but not all, tasks were done.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'only' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The warranty covers only manufacturing defects, not accidental damage.
quests.hint: A common mistake is placing this word right before the verb - instead, place it directly before the specific category it's limiting.
quests.explanation: Placing 'only' before 'covers' would wrongly suggest the warranty does nothing else at all. It belongs directly before 'manufacturing defects', the exact category being limited.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'fresh' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The bakery sells fresh bread every morning, along with pastries baked the day before.
quests.hint: A common mistake is letting this word seem to describe every item in the sentence - instead, keep it directly attached to the one item it actually describes.
quests.explanation: 'Fresh' describes only the bread, not the pastries mentioned later, which the second half of the sentence confirms were baked earlier. It sits directly before 'bread'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'certified' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The clinic employs certified nurses and several trainees still in school.
quests.hint: A common mistake is letting this word seem to describe both groups mentioned - instead, keep it attached only to the group it actually describes.
quests.explanation: 'Certified' describes only the nurses, not the trainees, which the rest of the sentence makes clear. It sits directly before 'nurses'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'imported' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The store stocks imported cheese alongside cheaper local brands.
quests.hint: As before, keep this word attached only to the item it actually describes, not the contrasting item later in the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Imported' describes only the cheese mentioned first, contrasted with the local brands later. It sits directly before 'cheese'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'wearing a name tag' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The employee wearing a name tag greeted the visitor at the front desk.
quests.hint: A common mistake is placing this phrase at the end of the sentence, where it could attach to the wrong person - instead, keep it right after the person it actually describes.
quests.explanation: 'Wearing a name tag' describes the employee, so it sits directly after 'employee'. Placing it at the end, near 'visitor', would incorrectly suggest the visitor was wearing the name tag.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'holding a clipboard' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The inspector holding a clipboard reviewed the construction site.
quests.hint: Keep this phrase right after the person it describes, not later in the sentence near a different noun.
quests.explanation: 'Holding a clipboard' describes the inspector, so it sits directly after 'inspector', not near 'construction site' at the end.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'wrapped in plastic' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The waiter served the sandwich wrapped in plastic to the customer at table five.
quests.hint: Attach this phrase to the object it actually describes, not to the person receiving it.
quests.explanation: 'Wrapped in plastic' describes the sandwich, not the customer, so it sits directly after 'sandwich'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'with the missing label' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The warehouse shipped the box with the missing label to the wrong address.
quests.hint: A common mistake is letting this phrase drift toward the end of the sentence, where it could seem to describe the address - instead, keep it right after the noun it actually describes.
quests.explanation: 'With the missing label' describes the box, not the address, so it sits directly after 'box'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'with a torn cover' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The library restored the book with a torn cover before returning it to the shelf.
quests.hint: Keep this phrase directly after the object it describes, not near the phrase about the shelf.
quests.explanation: 'With a torn cover' describes the book, so it sits directly after 'book', ahead of the phrase about returning it.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'with a cracked lens' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The technician replaced the camera with a cracked lens during the inspection.
quests.hint: Think about which object actually has the cracked lens, and attach the phrase directly to it.
quests.explanation: 'With a cracked lens' describes the camera being replaced, not a tool used to replace it, so it sits directly after 'camera'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'clearly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager clearly explained why the project was delayed.
quests.hint: In this mid-sentence position, the word describes how the explaining was done - place it directly before the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Clearly' sits before 'explained', describing the manner of the explanation. Note this differs from starting a sentence with 'Clearly,' which would instead comment on the whole statement.
quests.grammarRule: Adverb Scope - Manner vs Sentence Adverb

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'Obviously,' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Obviously, the team needed more time to finish.
quests.hint: At the front of the sentence, this word comments on the whole statement rather than describing a single action - place it there, followed by a comma.
quests.explanation: 'Obviously' opens the sentence as a comment on the entire statement, meaning 'it is obvious that...', a different job from a manner adverb placed mid-sentence.
quests.grammarRule: Adverb Scope - Manner vs Sentence Adverb

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'Honestly,' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Honestly, I don't think the plan will work.
quests.hint: At the front of the sentence, this word signals the speaker's own attitude toward the whole statement - place it there, followed by a comma.
quests.explanation: 'Honestly' opens the sentence, commenting on the speaker's sincerity about the whole claim, rather than describing how any single action was performed.
quests.grammarRule: Adverb Scope - Manner vs Sentence Adverb

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'that needed signing' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract that needed signing was left on the conference table.
quests.hint: A common mistake is moving this clause to the end of the sentence, where it could attach to the wrong noun - instead, keep it right after the noun it actually describes.
quests.explanation: 'That needed signing' describes the contract, not the table, so it sits directly after 'contract', not at the end of the sentence.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'who was assigned the case' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The detective who was assigned the case interviewed every witness personally.
quests.hint: Keep this clause right after the person it describes, not at the end near a different noun.
quests.explanation: 'Who was assigned the case' describes the detective, not the witnesses, so it sits directly after 'detective'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'which included several errors' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The report which included several errors was returned to the intern for revisions.
quests.hint: Attach this clause to the noun it actually describes, not to the person mentioned later.
quests.explanation: 'Which included several errors' describes the report, not the intern, so it sits directly after 'report'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'quickly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to quickly look up the word before the meeting.
quests.hint: This word belongs before the whole phrasal verb, not squeezed between its two parts - place it directly before 'look up'.
quests.explanation: 'Quickly' sits before the phrasal verb 'look up' as a unit. Splitting the phrasal verb itself, as in 'look quickly up', would sound unnatural.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'carefully' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Please carefully fill out every field on the form.
quests.hint: Place this word before the whole phrasal verb, not between its two parts.
quests.explanation: 'Carefully' sits before the phrasal verb 'fill out' as a unit, rather than splitting it into 'fill carefully out', which would sound awkward.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'thoroughly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The mechanic thoroughly checked over the engine before the road trip.
quests.hint: Apply the same rule: place this word before the whole phrasal verb, not between its two parts.
quests.explanation: 'Thoroughly' sits before the phrasal verb 'checked over' as a unit, avoiding the awkward split 'checked thoroughly over'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'Unfortunately,' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Unfortunately, the flight was cancelled after we had already checked in our bags.
quests.hint: This word comments on the entire main clause, not the smaller clause about checking in bags - place it at the very start of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Unfortunately' opens the sentence, commenting on the whole main clause ('the flight was cancelled'), not the subordinate clause about checking in bags.
quests.grammarRule: Sentence Adverb Placement Across Clause Boundaries

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'Apparently,' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Apparently, the meeting was moved to a different room without anyone being told.
quests.hint: Place this word at the start of the sentence, where it comments on the whole main clause rather than a smaller part of it.
quests.explanation: 'Apparently' opens the sentence, signaling that the entire main clause is based on secondhand information, not just the detail about not being told.
quests.grammarRule: Sentence Adverb Placement Across Clause Boundaries

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'Surprisingly,' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Surprisingly, the new intern finished the project ahead of schedule despite the tight deadline.
quests.hint: As before, this word comments on the whole main clause - place it at the very start of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Surprisingly' opens the sentence, commenting on the entire main clause, not just the detail about the tight deadline.
quests.grammarRule: Sentence Adverb Placement Across Clause Boundaries

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'from the finance team' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager who approved the request from the finance team left early.
quests.hint: This phrase describes where the request came from, not where the manager works - attach it directly after the noun it describes, inside the relative clause.
quests.explanation: 'From the finance team' describes the request, so it sits directly after 'request', correctly placed within the relative clause 'who approved the request'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'working carefully on the wiring' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The technician working carefully on the wiring finished ahead of schedule.
quests.hint: This phrase describes the technician - attach it directly after that noun, with the manner adverb correctly placed inside it.
quests.explanation: 'Working carefully on the wiring' sits directly after 'technician', with the adverb 'carefully' correctly placed before the verb it modifies within the phrase.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'to finish the proposal' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She stayed late to finish the proposal for the new client.
quests.hint: This phrase explains her purpose for staying late - place it after the main clause, before the phrase describing who the proposal is for.
quests.explanation: 'To finish the proposal' explains why she stayed late, sitting directly after 'stayed late', ahead of the phrase 'for the new client', which attaches to the proposal itself.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'that was submitted late' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The application that was submitted late was still reviewed by the committee.
quests.hint: Keep this clause right after the noun it describes, not drifting toward the end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'That was submitted late' describes the application, so it sits directly after 'application', not near 'committee' at the end.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'nearly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The store nearly sold out of the new product on launch day.
quests.hint: Recall the scope-sensitive placement rule from earlier in the course - place this word directly before the verb it modifies.
quests.explanation: 'Nearly' sits directly before 'sold out', showing the store came close to selling out completely but didn't quite.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'with the torn packaging' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The customer returned the item with the torn packaging for a refund.
quests.hint: Attach this phrase to the object it actually describes, not to the reason for the return.
quests.explanation: 'With the torn packaging' describes the item being returned, so it sits directly after 'item', ahead of the phrase explaining the reason for the return.
